questions.stem: In which state of matter is diffusion fastest, and why?

options.text: Solids, because the particles are packed closely and can pass energy quickly
Liquids, because the particles can move around each other
Gases, because the particles move faster and there is more space between them
Diffusion happens at the same rate in all states

questions.explanation: Diffusion is fastest in gases because gas particles move faster than particles in other states and there is more space between them, meaning fewer collisions to slow the particles down. Diffusion is slowest in solids because particles can only vibrate in fixed positions.

questions.stem: Which is a limitation of the simple particle model?

options.text: It cannot explain why gases can be compressed
It does not show the forces between particles or the internal structure of atoms
It only works for solids, not liquids or gases
It shows particles as being different sizes in different states

questions.explanation: The simple particle model has several limitations: particles are shown as solid spheres without internal structure, the forces between particles are not shown, all particles look the same regardless of type, and energy is not visible. Despite these limitations, it is very useful for explaining the basic properties of matter.
